(By Advocate: Sri. Kiran Pujar)
 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 27.09.2021 at about 12.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ED-7995 on the extreme left side of Tumkur - Bengaluru slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Kengal Kempohalli, Tumkur - Bengaluru NH-48 road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru at that time, driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-5121 which was driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life came from opposite side i.e., from Bengaluru - Tumkur road and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle by crossing the NH-48 road divider.

As a result of which he sustained grievous injuries and after the accident he was shifted to Nelamangala Government Hospital wherein he took first aid treatement, then he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, at the time of accident he was working as Senior Sales and Marketing Executive and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry.

The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation,
as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. In pursuance of duly service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court when it was held for appearance.
Thereafter he placed exparte.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-5121.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent No.2 has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 147, 149(2), 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of one day in lodging the complaint that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle /
petitioner who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid &
Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129228588/
2 effective DL as on the date of accident.

entities.text: Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the petitioner was also not possessing valid and effective DL on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.09.2021 at about 12.30 p.m., near Kengal Kempohalli, on Tumkur - Bengaluru (NH-48) road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District due to actionable negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-5121 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 18 were marked on his behalf.
The MRO of Sparsh Hospital is examined as PW.2.
Ex.P.19 to 22 were marked through him.

Dr.S.A.
Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Lady Curzon Hospital was examined as PW.3.
Ex.P.23 & 24 were marked through him.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 did not choose lead evidence.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by Mr. Ravi Kumar. K.B the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51- 5121 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 338 of IPC and u/s 56 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the insurance company has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any evidence to this effect.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129228588/
3 Reg.No.KA-51-5121.
10.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 drew the attention of this Court as to the delay in lodging the complaint.
Indeed there is delay of one day in lodging the complaint.

But when the injured was admitted to the hospital for taking treatment due to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, it was the bounden duty of the hospital authorities to send the MLC intimation to the concerned police station, who were duty bound to rush to the hospital, record the statement of the injured and register the case at the earliest.
For their fault petitioner cannot be blamed.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the lorry.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.

12. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i) Right humerus shaft fracture (ii) liver injuury (iii) Right kidney grade IV injury (iv) 4 th, 5th and 6th rib fracture.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

13. The Discharge summary issued by Sparsh hospital, Bengaluru which is marked at Ex.P.11 indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 26.09.2021 to 11.10.2021 (16 days in total).
During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : ORIF left humerus with plate and screws fixation.
14. It is the definite assertion of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled.

Therefore he examined an Orthopedic Surgeon by name Dr. S.A. Somashekar as PW.3 who deposed that on clinical examination, he found that the petitioner has 34% disability to the right upper limb and 17% whole body physical disability.
15. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD & LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
Now it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.
As per the averments made in his evidence affidavit, at the time of accident the petitioner was working as Senior Sales and Marketing Executive and thereby earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
To substantiate the same he has produced his Appointment letter, Annual salary package, Salary certificate and Account statement which are marked at Ex's.P.14 to 18 respectively.

On perusal of Ex.P.16 salary slip for the month of April-2022 wherein it discloses that he was joined his duties on 02.12.2019 and further it discloses that the accident occurred on 27.09.2021 and the pay slip for the month of April-2022 manifestly clear that he was continued his job in the same company.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.17 Bank account clearly discloses that the said statement is from 11.06.2021 to 20.9.2021, but the accident occurred on 27.09.2021.
On perusal of the same it reveals that he has received salary for the months of May -2021, June-2021, July-2021, August-2021.
It clearly shows he intentionally not produced September-2021 month bank statement before the court.
Be that as it may, the petitioner admitted in the course of his cross-examination that he has continued his job.

Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129228588/
4
The relevant portion is culled out as follows : He was working in Thirumala Milk Diary.
The payment was credited to his bank account.
He further admitted that the accident occurred on 27.09.2021 and Ex.P.16 is pay slip for the month of April-2022.
To put it differently, the author of Ex.P.16 is not examined before the Court.
Hence no credence can be attached to the contents made therein.
The discussion supra goes to show petitioner has neither been terminated from his job on account of accidental injuries nor he has suffered any financial loss during the laid-up period.
Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the head 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
It is also clear that the claimant does not have any functional disability.
Under these circumstances the question of calculating the loss of future income due to disability also does not arise.

Relying upon the ratio laid down in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 (Subhash V/s The New India Assurance Co.Ltd), no compensation is awarded under the head of 'Loss of future income due to disability'.
16.

sentences.text: However it should be remembered that the petitioner has suffered physical disability to the extent of 17% to the whole body.

Placing reliance upon the decision reported in ILR 2015 KAR 167 (Dr.Yeshwant Dongre V/s Salman Rasheed & others), I deem it just & proper to award a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards the disability suffered by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
Petitioner has suffered multiple fracture injuries.
As such, necessarily he had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus, this tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The age of the petitioner was 33 years at the time of accident.
Unfortunately, at such young age he has suffered whole body disability to the extent of 17%, with which he has to lead his entire life.
Therefore, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.60,000/- under this head.
19. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 16 days is proved with the help of Ex.P.11 Discharge summary.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.24,000/- (1,500 X 16) is awarded under this head.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is categorically admitted during the course of cross examination of PW.1 is that, "It is true that, the medical bill was reimbursed and I have paid only amount of Rs.46,963/-.".
Hence the said words clearly discloses entire medical bills are reimbursed from insurance company and not by petitioner.
Further on perusal of Final bill (Sl.No.17) it clearly shows that the said bill is computer generated bill, but in the said bill it is overwritten the same by using pen.
Further it is mentioned in the bottom of the bill patient due amount (INR) is shown as NIL.
Hence no amount is awarded under this head.

Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129228588/
5 21.
FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.40,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of income during laid-up : - Nil - period & loss of future income due to disability 2

Towards Disability : 1,00,000-00 3 Pain and sufferings : 60,000-00 4 Loss of future amenities & : 60,000-00 happiness 5 Attendant charges,
extra nutritious : 24,000-00 food & conveyance charges 6 Medical Expenses : - Nil - 7
Future Medical Expenses : 40,000-00  Total 2,84,000-00 23.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
24. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-5121 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,84,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Mohan Naik.S vs Satish.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129228588/
6

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/ RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
